newsitem.title: UK: UK tube sale seen raising net 0.6-1.5 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: UK tube sale seen raising net 0.6-1.5 bln pounds.

text.p: Britain could raise between 600 million and 1.5 billion pounds ($2.41 billion) in net proceeds if it decided to sell the London Underground network, according to Steven Norris, a former transport minister.

Norris, who has been involved informally with government studies into a possible sale and is now part of a team in the ruling Conservative Party preparing its election manifesto, said on Wednesday he understood the sale proceeds figure was calculated excluding the cost of funding necessary investments.
The gross proceeds figure was put at between 1.4 billion and 2.5 billion pounds, he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He also said that the government was strongly considering an RPI(retail price index)-linked formula which would control Tube fares through a cap either at or below the rate of inflation and the type of RPI- formula used by other utility regulators.

"There has to be an absolute guarantee of a price cap," said Norris. "The government is certainly looking at an RPI or RPI minus tupe of formula." He said he believed the government was also looking at a way of safeguarding service levels.
Norris said he had been informally involved in the talks due his knowledge of the network after his tenure at the Department of Transport where he was responsible for London Underground.

He said recent press reports putting the sale figure at around 13 billion pounds were wrong. "This refers to the cost of building or replacing the entire network rather than the value of the business," he said.

"It does not take into account the liabilities which include very considerable outstanding repairs and the renewals bill." He saw this bill at around 2.0 billion pounds ($3.21 billion). ($1=.6237 Pound)
